title: API Management APIs, Products, and Subscriptions
description: Learn how APIM organizes APIs into products and uses subscriptions to control access.

data.text: APIM uses three core concepts: APIs (your operations), products (groupings of APIs), and subscriptions (keys that grant access to products).
An API represents one or more operations. A product is a collection of APIs you offer to a specific audience. A subscription is how a consumer gets access to a product.

data.title: Product Types
items: Public — visible to all developers on the portal
Private — visible only to invited developers
Restricted — requires administrator approval before access

data.title: Import and Publish an API with Azure CLI
data.content: Import an OpenAPI definition and add it to a product.
data.code:
# Import an API from an OpenAPI spec
az apim api create   --resource-group myRG   --service-name myApim   --api-id weather-api   --display-name "Weather API"   --path weather   --specification-format OpenApi   --specification-path https://myapi.example.com/openapi.json

# Create a product
az apim product create   --resource-group myRG   --service-name myApim   --product-id weather-product   --display-name "Weather Product"   --subscription-required true

# Add the API to the product
az apim product api add   --resource-group myRG   --service-name myApim   --product-id weather-product   --api-id weather-api

data.title: Publish Your First API
data.description: Import an OpenAPI spec into APIM, create a product, and subscribe a test user.
steps: Import an existing OpenAPI definition as a new API.
Create a product named 'Partner APIs' with subscription required.
Add the API to the product.
Create a subscription key and test a request through the APIM gateway.
data.expectedOutcome: You can call the API through the APIM gateway using the subscription key.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Products group APIs for specific audiences.
Subscriptions control who can call which products.
data.takeaway: Organize APIs into products so you can offer different tiers (free, basic, premium) to different consumers.
